open_obligations: Note that Bai et al. define Scaling Supervision for training systems, not for checking exploratory actions as they are made.
Check whether AI feedback could judge which actions are genuinely risky, the key challenge Amodei et al. name.
Check whether Bai et al. warn that less human feedback makes untested deployment easier.
out.other_title: Human checking of risky exploration runs into the scalable oversight problem
out.rationale: Amodei et al. note human checking of risky actions runs into scalable oversight because the agent may need too many exploratory actions or may need to make them too fast for humans to judge. Bai et al. use the term 'Scaling Supervision' for techniques that leverage AI to help humans more efficiently supervise AI, making it possible to train systems to behave in desirable ways (for example, to be helpful and honest); the setting is training systems, not checking an RL agent's exploratory actions.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether AI assistance can reduce the amount of human oversight needed when too many decisions need checking
